what_it_does: A Key-Value SSD (solid-state drive) is a storage device that speaks the language of databases directly — you hand it a key (like a name) and it stores or retrieves the associated value (like a record) without the operating system having to manage a separate file system layer. Existing designs assume values are much larger than keys, but some real workloads use long keys, and that causes the internal bookkeeping tables to balloon in size without bound. AnyKey fixes this by separating the bookkeeping entry for a key from the full key text itself — storing only a compact fingerprint (a short hash) in the main index, while the full key lives elsewhere — so the index stays a fixed, predictable size no matter how long keys get.
